commentary: Something twenty tiles west, out past the lot. I have seen it, I am noting it, and it is not between me and these shelves. I am not switching the alarm off, I am just telling it I heard it.

action: press 'j' -- step one tile south toward the shop shelving
commentary: Now south, one step, toward the racks. Slow and deliberate; I do not have a second back.

action: press '!' -- turn safe mode off so movement inside the shop is no longer blocked
commentary: The alarm will not let me cross my own room over something twenty tiles away and outside. Off. I would rather trust my ears, which have not been wrong yet this week, than a bell that rings at everything.

action: press '.' -- stand still for one turn and listen
commentary: Stop. Stand still, count to one, and listen properly instead of shoving at the room. If it is coming across that lot I will hear it before I see it.

action: press '!' as shift+1 -- actually turn safe mode off this time
commentary: The alarm is still on and it has been eating every move I make. Off, properly. My ears are better than it is.

action: press 'j' -- step one tile south off the counter aisle
commentary: South, one step. The racks are two rows in front of me and I want to see what is actually on them before I want anything else.

action: press 'j' -- step one tile further south, up against the shop shelving
commentary: Again. Close enough to put a hand on it.

action: press 'e' -- start an examine, which asks for a direction
commentary: There is a rack right in front of my knees with gloves on it. Gloves are not on my list but hands are how I do everything, so I will look properly.

action: press 'j' -- examine the rack immediately to the south
commentary: The rack below me. Let us see what a golf shop keeps at knee height.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, back behind the shop counter
commentary: The rack is a picture of gloves behind glass and it is not giving me anything. Back behind the counter, where I can see the doorway and nothing can come at me from two sides at once.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: I am not walking out into a lot with a runner on it, empty-handed, at eight in the morning. I am going to sit behind this counter, keep my back straight against something solid, and listen to the building.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while' from the wait menu
commentary: My father's watch has an alarm in it. Twenty-two years of shift work and I never once needed it to tell me when to get up, but I am glad of it now.

action: press '3' -- wait five minutes
commentary: Five minutes. Long enough for whatever is out west to walk on past, short enough that I have not thrown away my morning. You do not open a valve you have not listened to first.

action: press 'j' -- step one tile south, down the aisle toward the low display shelving
commentary: Nothing came for me in five minutes. Whatever that ant was hitting, it was not this building. Down the aisle then. Those low racks along the south wall are the only thing in here I have not put my hands on yet.

action: press 'e' -- examine, awaiting a direction
commentary: Glass and steel shelving, the kind that gets bolted down. If there is anything on it worth carrying it will be sitting right there in front of me.

action: press 'j' -- examine the tile to the south, the display shelf under the gloves
commentary: The one under the gloves first. Work gloves I can use. My hands are the only tools I brought out of that house with me and I would rather not open them up on broken glass.

action: press 'x' -- look around
commentary: Nothing came of that, so I will stop guessing at it and look at the thing properly. Twenty-two years of being handed a fault report written by somebody who never went and looked. I am not going to be that.

action: press 'j' -- move the looking cursor one tile south, onto the shelf
commentary: Eyes on it. Whatever is on that rack, I want to read it off the shelf and not off a picture in my head.

action: press Escape -- close the looking cursor
commentary: Golfing gloves, a pair, and they will not fit me properly. Fine. Poor fit beats bare knuckles on glass and metal, and I have done worse with worse.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: Reach in and take them. I have been standing in a shop for five minutes being too polite to rob it.

action: press 'j' -- pick up from the tile to the south, the rack under the glass
commentary: South. The rack right in front of my knees.

action: press 'W' as shift+w -- wear the highlighted item straight off the rack
commentary: Straight onto my hands. There is no sense carrying a thing I am going to want in the next hour anyway, and my knuckles are the first part of me that is going to meet something sharp.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west along the aisle
commentary: Gloves will not open a door and they will not break a window. There is something dark sitting on two of the racks further down and I want to know what it is.

action: press 'b' -- step southwest, into the gap between two blocks of shelving
commentary: Into the gap between the blocks. Standing in here I can reach four faces of shelf without walking, and my back thanks me for every step I do not take.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: Right then. What is on the low shelf.

action: press 'b' -- pick up from the tile to the southwest
commentary: The lower rack, to my left and down. That is where the heavy things live in any shop I have ever been in.

action: press 'W' as shift+w -- wear one of the two golf caps off the lower rack
commentary: Golf caps. Two of them. I will take one on my head because it is the twentieth of May and I am going to be outside in the sun by noon, and I have never once in my life owned a hat I chose.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window and leave the second cap on the rack
commentary: One is enough. I have nothing to put a spare in. Until I find a bag, everything I take has to go on my body or in my hands, and I am keeping my hands free.

action: press 'y' -- step northwest, back up out of the gap
commentary: Back out of the gap and along. There are two more blocks of shelving west of me and something dark on both of them.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: Straight down the middle of the floor. I keep the glass on my left and the wall on my right and I do not turn my back on the doorway.

action: press 'b' -- step southwest into the second gap between shelving blocks
commentary: Down into the next gap. Same trick as before, four faces from one place.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: The dark thing on the upper shelf, east side of this gap.

action: press 'l' -- pick up from the tile to the east
commentary: Right in front of me at chest height. Whatever it is, it is heavy enough that they did not hang it up.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window; another cap, no use to me
commentary: Another cap. This whole wall is hats and gloves. Somebody made a living selling people things they already had.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: There is something on the bottom shelf on the far side of this gap that is not cloth. It has links in it.

action: press 'b' -- pick up from the tile to the southwest
commentary: Bottom shelf, left and down. Links means steel, and steel is the first honest thing I have seen in this building.

action: press 'W' as shift+w -- wear the golf bag
commentary: A golf bag. On the bottom shelf, behind the hats, where nobody looked. That is a strap over one shoulder and a hole I can put things in, and it is worth more to me this morning than everything else in this building stacked together. Onto my back it goes.

action: press 'y' -- step northwest out of the shelf gap onto the open floor
commentary: Out of the gap and onto the open floor. There is something long and thin lying on the next block of shelving along, and further down this wall there is a red box with a slot in it that I would recognise blind. That is a drinks machine. That is water.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: One thing at a time. The long one first.

action: press 'b' -- pick up from the tile to the southwest
commentary: Down and to the left. The bag on my back gives me forty litres to put things in now, which is forty litres more than I had at breakfast.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window; leave the second bag
commentary: Another bag, the same as the one on my back. I cannot wear two and the second will not go inside the first. It stays where it is and I will remember it is there, which is worth as much as carrying it.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west along the open floor
commentary: West along the wall, in the clear strip between the shelving and the glass. Slow, because slow is what I have got.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: Past the end of the second block. My back tells me about every one of these steps but it has been telling me that for six years and I have not listened yet.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: Three more and I am level with the pink stuff on the low shelves. Food, if I am lucky. Sweets, if I am not.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: Keep going. Nothing has come through that doorway behind me and I would rather be finished in here before something does.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: Level with them now, or near enough.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: The red machine is five along and one up from me. There is a taller one beside it in grey and something cylindrical between them. I will get to all three.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west
commentary: First the low shelves with the pink on them. Food comes before drink only because it is closer.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west, level with the pink goods
commentary: There. Level with them.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: Whatever they were selling to people between the ninth and the tenth hole, I will take it.

action: press 'j' -- pick up from the tile to the south
commentary: Straight down, the shelf at my knees.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window; leave the golf shoes
commentary: Golf shoes. Spikes in the sole for standing on wet grass. I have steel toes on my feet that have done twenty-two years on a mill floor and they are staying on. This whole wall is hats and shoes. Nobody in here was selling anything you could drink.

action: press 'h' -- step one tile west, level below the red machine
commentary: Then it is the red machine. Everything else in this room is cloth.

action: press 'e' -- examine nearby terrain or furniture
commentary: Have a proper look at it before I put a hand on it. Twenty-two years of that habit and it has never cost me anything.

action: press 'y' -- examine the tile to the northwest, the red machine
commentary: Up and to the left.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: Nothing in here answers to being examined, which tells me these three things against the wall are not fixtures. They are somebody's property, standing where somebody left them. A red box with a slot, a grey one behind it, and a cylinder between the two.

action: press 'y' -- pick up from the tile to the northwest
commentary: Up and to the left. The red one.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window; leave the glass shards
commentary: Somebody got here before me. The front of it is stoved in and there are forty-one pieces of glass on the floor where the bottles used to stand. I am not the first person to have had this idea and I will not be the last. Nothing to drink.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north
commentary: One step up. There is a cylinder standing between the two machines and a cylinder that size is either gas or water. I would take either one of those.

action: press 'e' -- examine nearby terrain or furniture
commentary: Now try it again from here. If any of these three is a fixture with a tap or a valve on it, this is where the game will tell me so.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: No valves, no taps, nothing with a handle on it. Then they are things lying about, and things lying about can be lifted.

action: press 'y' -- pick up from the tile to the northwest, the cylinder
commentary: The cylinder. Up and left.

action: press Escape -- close the pickup window; leave the glass
commentary: Three machines against that wall and all three of them opened up before I ever got here. Forty-one pieces of glass and nothing to put in a bottle. Right. I know what this building is now: it sold hats.

action: press 'i' -- open the inventory
commentary: Right. Stop and count what I have got, because a list is the only thing that has ever stopped me making the same mistake twice. Everything on this list I have had for less than ten minutes except the watch.

action: press Escape -- close the inventory
commentary: A shirt, a bra, shorts, jeans, socks and boots. A hat, a pair of gloves that do not fit, and a bag with forty-three litres still empty in it. A phone charged full and nobody to call with it. Forty dollars in a wallet, which is the funniest thing I have read all week. And my father's watch on my left wrist, which is the only item on that whole list worth anything this morning, because it is the only one of them still telling me the truth.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: I have no water, no weapon and no way out of this town on foot with this back. What I do have is a building with brick on three sides and both doors shut. So I am going to do the one thing that costs nothing: sit down in it and let the day go past.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: A while, then. Not a fixed job with a finish time on it, just a while.

action: press '7' -- wait three hours
commentary: Three hours. That takes me to the middle of the day with the sun high and the whole lot outside lit up, and I would rather look at that parking lot in full light than in this flat morning glare.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- answer Yes, stop waiting
commentary: Gargling. Something out there is gargling, and that is not a noise a living person makes with a throat that works. Four minutes of sitting still is all I got. Yes, I am stopping. You do not keep your eyes shut when you can hear it breathing.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu again
commentary: Nothing came through the wall. Whatever was gargling is outside on the tarmac with brick between us and the door shut, and by the sound of it it has got something else to be busy with. I have no weapon and no legs to run on. Back to the only plan I have.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: A while.

action: press 'k' -- wait until night
commentary: Until dark. Near enough twelve hours of sitting on a shop floor with my back against something solid, which is more rest than I have had in six years of nights. If those two want to tear at each other all day out there they are welcome to it.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore this distraction and continue waiting
commentary: Growling now. Same two, same argument, same side of the same wall. I have looked once and I am not going to jump up every time one of them makes a noise, or I will spend the whole day standing. Ignore it and sit.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- answer Yes, stop waiting
commentary: That is not a noise any more. I can see it. Black armour, helmet, moving like it still knows how, and it has just finished pulling a dog-sized ant apart with three others helping. I have gloves and a hat. Yes. I am up.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, away from the glass shopfront
commentary: Ten tiles. That is the whole width of the parking lot and it is looking at me through a shop window, because the entire south face of this building is glass and I have been sitting in front of it like a display. North. Away from the glass, into the brick.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north
commentary: Two steps and I am at the back wall of this room. It is brick and it is between me and the tarmac and that is the best sentence I have said to myself all morning.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: It cannot see me from here. Brick at my back, three dead machines down my left side, and the whole width of the shop floor between me and that window. This corner is the best thing this building has given me and it gave it to me by accident.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: So. A while.

action: press 'k' -- wait until night
commentary: Until dark, then. I have no water to ration and no food to eke out, so there is nothing to do with the daylight except waste it somewhere it cannot see me. Twelve hours. My back can have them.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- answer Yes, stop waiting
commentary: Fifty seconds and it is in my eyeline again. So the corner is not as clever as I thought it was -- there is a line from that window to this floor and I am standing on it. Yes. Stop. Look properly this time.

action: press 'l' -- step one tile east
commentary: It has not come any closer. It is stood out on the tarmac where the ant died, eleven tiles off, and it has not taken a step toward the glass. Fine. But this whole room is a window and no amount of sitting still is going to change that. There is a doorway through to the back.

action: press 'l' -- step one tile east
commentary: Two. Keeping the shelving between me and the front where I can.

action: press 'l' -- step one tile east, onto the green carpet
commentary: Onto the green. Somebody carpeted a strip of this place in fake grass so the members could practise their putting indoors when it rained. I am walking across it in steel toes and I do not feel one bit sorry.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, through into the back room
commentary: North, through the gap. Away from the glass.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile further north into the unlit interior
commentary: Through. It is dark in here and there is no window in any wall I can see. There are four chairs off to my right where people used to sit and wait for a tee time, and a door in the far wall. No glass. Nothing out there has a line on me now.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: This will do. It is not a room with a door I can shut behind me, which is what I actually wanted, but it is a room with no window in it, and I will take the second one today.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: A while.

action: press 'k' -- wait until night
commentary: Until dark. Twelve hours sat on a carpet tile in the dark with my back against a brick wall, and I have had worse shifts than that for money.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore this distraction and continue waiting
commentary: Groaning, from the far side of a brick wall it cannot see through. It has lost me. Good. Ignore it and let the clock run, because the only thing I have got working in my favour today is that it gets dark at the end.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore this distraction and continue waiting
commentary: And there it is. Not the zombie, not the ant. My own hands. I have had a packet in my shirt pocket every day for thirty years and this morning I have got a bag, a hat and no cigarettes, and my body has just noticed. There is nothing to be done about it and nothing out there to be bought, so it can want. Keep sitting.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- answer Yes, stop waiting
commentary: Half past three in the afternoon and there is another one of those ants, and this time I can see it. That is not the thing that has changed though. My mouth has gone. Very thirsty, and I have sat on a carpet tile for seven hours doing nothing about it. That was a mistake and it is mine. Up.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north toward the door in the far wall
commentary: Three things in my eyeline and not one of them is a tap. An ant to the west, a wild turkey somewhere off to the south east, and between me and the ant something the game has the decency to call a small meat cocoon, which means the ants have been carrying things in here and wrapping them up. That is a larder. I am not going west. There is a door in the north wall and doors in the north walls of clubhouses lead to lavatories, and a lavatory has a cistern in it.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north
commentary: Two. My tongue is stuck to the roof of my mouth and it has been getting worse for seven hours while I sat congratulating myself on a brick wall.

action: press 'u' -- step northeast into the closed metal door, which opens it
commentary: There. A steel door in the back wall, painted the same grey as every service door I have ever gone through with a spanner in my hand. On the other side of that there is either a corridor, a lavatory, or the outside, and two of those three are worth having. Get it open.

action: press 'u' -- step northeast through the opened doorway
commentary: Wood. Not steel. I called it wrong from four feet away in bad light and I will write that down, because the day I stop correcting myself is the day I put my hand somewhere I should not. Through.

action: press 'y' -- step northwest out into the yard
commentary: Not a lavatory. Outside. A staff yard with bay lines painted on it, which means deliveries came in this way, and the sun is straight down on the back of my neck. But there is something white and square sitting against the wall four bays over, and white and square and man-made is a basin, a cooler or a fridge, and every one of those has held water at some point in its life.

action: press 'y' -- step northwest
commentary: Two. Nothing on this side of the building is moving. Whatever is out front is still out front.

action: press 'y' -- step northwest, level with the white fixture
commentary: Three. It is right there on my left now, tucked in against the brick where the bins would go.

action: press 'e' -- examine nearby terrain or furniture
commentary: Now then. If that is a basin there will be a tap on it, and if there is a tap on it there may still be something in the pipe above it, because water does not run downhill out of a building when the pumps stop -- it sits in the dead leg waiting for somebody to open the lowest tap in the run. And this is the lowest tap in the run.

action: press 'g' -- pick up items from a nearby tile
commentary: It is not a basin. It is two white boxes stacked against the brick with an orange mark stencilled on the front of each and something dark sitting in them. Orange stencil on white means somebody wanted it noticed from a distance.

action: press 'h' -- pick up from the tile to the west
commentary: The near one.

action: press 'm' -- view the map
commentary: Two dead ends in a row and my mouth is worse than it was an hour ago. Stop poking at boxes and think. This is a golf course. Golf courses have ponds on them -- they dig them for the drainage and then call them water hazards and charge you for the ball. If there is one within walking distance of this building then there is water, and I would drink out of a ditch today. Get my bearings.

action: press Escape -- close the map
commentary: There it is. Fryeburg, and I am at the bottom left corner of it with the course on my east and the woods on my west. And there is water -- three ponds that I can see, and the nearest one is two squares off to the south west through the trees. Two squares. That is the better part of a mile on a back that has been shouting at me since eight this morning, and it is half three in the afternoon. I would get there at dusk, in the open, with nowhere to sit down at the other end. No. I know where it is now, and knowing is most of it. I go at first light.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast, back toward the doorway
commentary: Back to the door. Three steps south east and I am at it.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast
commentary: Two. The sun is off the wall now and the yard has gone cool, which means the afternoon is turning.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast, into the open doorway
commentary: Three. Standing in the doorway with one hand on the frame.

action: press 'j' -- step south, through and inside
commentary: And in. That is me back inside brick with the yard behind me.

action: press 'c' -- close a door
commentary: And now the thing I have wanted since I woke up in this building, and it turns out it was hanging on a hinge in the back wall the whole time.

action: press 'k' -- close the door to the north, behind her
commentary: Shut it. There. A room with a door that closes. I have a hat, a pair of gloves that do not fit, a bag with nothing in it, my father's watch, and a door I can shut, and at eight o'clock this morning I had four of those and did not know where the fifth was.

action: press 'j' -- step south, back off the threshold (correcting the previous line: the door went shut and then I walked straight back into it and knocked it open again)
commentary: I have to take that back. It did shut -- I felt it go -- and then I put my own boot straight back through it and knocked it open again, and stood there congratulating myself in a doorway with the yard behind me. That is what a day with no water does to a person. Off the threshold. Properly, this time.

action: press 'c' -- close the door
commentary: Now shut it, and then stand still afterwards like somebody with sense.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, back to the tile beside the doorway (correcting again: the earlier north press only pushed the door open, it never moved me, so my step south then took me out of arm's reach of it)
commentary: Take that back as well, and take it back properly this time, because I have now got it wrong twice in a row about a door. I never walked into it. I pushed it open from where I stood without moving my feet an inch, and then I stepped back off it and put myself out of arm's reach, and then I stood there trying to shut a door that was two paces away. Read the thing in front of you, Delphine. One step north.

action: press 'c' -- close the door
commentary: Now. Shut.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: Right. Door shut, brick on the other three sides, and nothing in this room but me and a carpet tile. I have got about five hours of daylight I cannot use and a mile to walk in the morning on a back that will not thank me for either.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: A while.

action: press 'k' -- wait until night
commentary: Until dark, then sleep, then walk. That is the whole plan and it is the first one I have had all day that does not depend on finding something in a cupboard.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore this distraction and continue waiting
commentary: My hands again. They can shake. There is not a cigarette inside a mile of this building and if there were I would trade it for a cup of water without thinking about it, so there is nothing here to decide. Ignore it. Let the light go.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- answer Yes, stop waiting
commentary: That is the ant, not a noise, and there is a wrapped-up parcel of meat somewhere on the west side of this building that says it did not come in through the front door. Stop. Find out where it is before it finds out where I am.

action: press 'k' -- press north into the closed door, which opens it
commentary: A nearby corpse rises and moves towards you. That is the sentence. One of the things that pack left on the tarmac has got back up and it is coming, and the ant is off my south west corner, and I am stood in a box with a carpet tile and no weapon in it. I do not fight things. I have never in my life hit anything that was not a seized nut with a hammer. Out the back.

action: press 'k' -- step north, into the open doorway
commentary: Through the frame.

action: press 'k' -- step north, out into the yard
commentary: And out. Yard behind the building, bay lines under my boots, and the whole brick shell of the place now stood between me and both of them.

action: press 'c' -- close the door behind her
commentary: Shut it behind me. It will not stop either of them for long but it will cost them time, and time is the only currency I have got that has not already run out today.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north, away from the door
commentary: Now walk. Not run, because I cannot, and not far, because I cannot do that either. Just far enough that whatever comes through that door has to look for me instead of finding me.

action: press 'k' -- step one tile north
commentary: Two bays out. The wind has got up a bit -- light breeze off the course, and it is the first thing all day that has felt like weather instead of heat.

action: press 'u' -- step northeast across the yard
commentary: North east, out along the bays and away from that door.

action: press 'u' -- step northeast
commentary: Four. Nothing behind me yet.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast, toward the parked cars
commentary: Cars. Three of them, sat in the staff bays along the back wall with their seats still in them, and I have walked past this whole afternoon looking in cupboards for water like a woman who has never held a spanner. There is a windscreen washer bottle on every car ever built. There is a reservoir under every bonnet. There is a tank in a boot if somebody was carrying one. That is my trade sat there in three lumps of painted steel and I nearly slept through it.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast
commentary: Two. Twenty-two years on the steam side and the first useful thought I have had today came from a car park.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast
commentary: Three, and level with the bays now.

action: press 'l' -- step east toward the nearest car
commentary: East along the row. Red one first, it is the closest.

action: press 'e' -- examine nearby terrain or furniture
commentary: Right up against it now. Red saloon, seats still in it, and I can see straight into the cabin. Let us see what it says for itself.

action: press 'l' -- examine the tile to the east, the front of the red car
commentary: East. The front of it.

action: press 'e' -- choose 'Examine vehicle'
commentary: Examine vehicle. That is the whole of my working life in two words and I have never been so pleased to read them.

action: press Escape -- close the vehicle panel
commentary: It is a golf cart. Electric motor, forty-five kilowatts safe and fifty flat out, and the panel says the motor is usable. One large storage battery, fifty thousand of capacity, sat at nineteen percent. Four bench seats and four ten-inch wheels and a steerable mount at the front. Nineteen percent of a battery that size will not take me to the coast but it will take me a mile to a pond and a mile back with something in the bag, and it will do it without asking my spine for permission. That is the first machine I have put my hands on since the buses stopped and it is a toy for carrying golf clubs, and I could sit down on this tarmac and cry about it.

action: press 'l' -- step east, onto the cart
commentary: Get aboard. If I am going to spend a night out of doors I would rather spend it sat on a bench seat with my back supported than flat on a car park, and I would rather be sat in the thing I intend to start in the morning.

action: press 'l' -- step east again, onto a bench seat
commentary: Onto the seat proper.

action: press 'u' -- step northeast onto open tarmac beside the cart (correcting the previous line: the bodywork stopped me and I never reached the seat)
commentary: And that is three times today I have said a thing before I checked it. I did not get on. I walked straight into the bodywork twice and stood there talking about bench seats. The panel is solid down that whole side -- of course it is, it is the front quarter. Round the nose of it and in from the top.

action: press 'n' -- step southeast, onto the cart's bench seat
commentary: In. Sat down.

action: press '^' as shift+6 -- control vehicle
commentary: Nineteen percent showing on the panel in front of me, and it is a battery reading, not a damage reading -- there is charge in this thing. And it is half past three in the afternoon with five hours of daylight left. I am not sitting here until dawn nursing a dry mouth when there is a motor under me and a pond two squares away. Find the controls.

action: press 's' -- turn on the engine
commentary: Turn on the engine. Three words. I have read those words on a hundred method statements and signed the bottom of most of them, and I have never once wanted to see them as much as I want to see them now. Go on.

action: press 'h' -- west, to see whether the cart will move under power
commentary: It started. It turned over and it caught and there is a motor running under this seat, and the first noise I have heard all day that a person built on purpose is coming out of a golf cart in a staff car park in Fryeburg. West. Facing two seventy already. Let us see if it will go.

action: press 'l' -- east, trying to shift across to the next bench seat
commentary: Nothing. Not a foot, not a reading on the speed, not even a refusal -- I pushed west and the cart simply did not care. And now I look properly at what is in front of my knees there is nothing in front of my knees. No wheel, no column, no pedal. I am sat in a passenger seat with a motor running behind me. Try the next one along.

action: press '^' as shift+6 -- control vehicle, from the second seat
commentary: Moved across. Four hundred and eleven of effort to slide one seat over with a bag on my back, which tells you everything about the state of me. Now ask it again from here.

action: press 's' -- turn off the engine
commentary: Same three lines from this seat as from the last one. Examine it, remember where it is, turn the engine off. That is all it will let me do, from either seat, and I have now asked it twice. There is no steering on this cart. Somebody has taken the column and the pedals out of it, or it never had them, and either way I have got a motor, a battery and four wheels and no way on God's earth to point them. So turn it off. Nineteen percent is nineteen percent and I am not going to stand here burning it to keep myself company.

action: press '|' as shift+backslash -- open the wait menu
commentary: So this is the night then. A bench seat in a golf cart with a dead battery I am not allowed to spend, in a walled yard behind a shop that sells hats, with the door shut on whatever is walking about inside it. My mouth is a disgrace and my hands want a cigarette and I am forty-seven years old.

action: press 'w' -- choose 'Wait a while'
commentary: A while.

action: press 'k' -- wait until night
commentary: Until dark. Then I sleep in this seat, and at first light I put one boot in front of the other and walk to that pond, and I carry back as much of it as this bag will hold. That is the job. It is a rubbish job and it is mine.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore this distraction and continue waiting
commentary: My hands again. They can want. Ignore it and let the sun go down.

action: press '$' as shift+4 -- sleep
commentary: Five to eight and the light has gone off the wall. Clear night, bit of a breeze, waxing crescent coming up over the course. I am down to seventy on my feet, my mouth has been a write-off since three, and I have not slept properly in six years -- ask anybody who has worked a night shift next to me. I am going to lie back on a bench seat in a golf cart that will not go anywhere and I am going to try anyway, because the walk starts at first light and I would like to be able to do it.

action: press 'S' as shift+s -- choose 'Yes, and save game before sleeping'
commentary: Yes. Lie back, shut my eyes and let tomorrow be tomorrow's problem. I have never been any good at this part -- I have not had a full night since the back went -- but I am going to give it an honest go, because a woman who cannot walk in the morning is a woman who does not drink in the morning.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- choose plain 'Yes.' (the previous press of 'S' was not accepted and left the prompt standing)
commentary: Yes. Enough deciding for one day. Eyes shut.

action: press '8' -- set the alarm to wake up in 8 hours
commentary: It is asking me if I want the alarm. Thirty years I have carried this watch and never once needed the thing, and tonight I do. Eight hours puts me at about four in the morning, and the light comes up at about four. That is not a coincidence, that is arithmetic, and it is the first bit of arithmetic that has gone my way since I woke up. Eight hours. Set it.

action: press 'I' as shift+i -- ignore the withdrawals and keep trying to fall asleep
commentary: Of course. Of course that is what wants me awake -- not the ant, not the thing walking about in the shop, not the dry mouth. Thirty years of a packet in my shirt pocket and it has picked tonight to send the bill in. No. I am not getting up for it. Lie still and let it pass, the same as every other night I have lain awake since the back went. Ignore it.

action: press 'C' as shift+c -- continue trying to fall asleep, and don't ask again
commentary: You have trouble sleeping. Yes. I know. I have had trouble sleeping since the twelfth of March six years ago when I picked up the wrong end of a gearbox casing on my own because the other fitter had gone for his break, and I have not had a full night since. I do not need telling and I do not need asking again. Keep trying, and stop putting the question to me every twenty minutes.

action: press Escape -- dismiss the popup that came up on waking
commentary: Ten to ten in the morning. I set that alarm for four and I have slept through it, through the light coming up, through whatever went past this yard in the night, and I have woken up on a bench seat with my mouth shut like a drawer and my whole right side seized solid. Friday the twenty-first of May. I have been alive one day in this and I am worse off than I was at breakfast yesterday -- dehydrated now, not just thirsty, and hungry with it. But I am alive, I slept, and the pond has not moved.

action: press 'S' as shift+s -- Save and quit
commentary: Right. Up. Bag on, hat on, gloves on, and my father's watch reading ten to ten on a Friday morning in Fryeburg, Maine. One mile of somebody's golf course between me and the first drink of water I will have had in a day and a half, and I know exactly which way it is because I stood in a car park yesterday afternoon and worked it out instead of guessing. I have a plan and I have something to carry it in. Yesterday morning I had neither. Off we go.

action: press 'Y' as shift+y -- confirm Save and quit
commentary: Yes. Shut the book on the twentieth of May. Delphine Ouellette, forty-seven, of no fixed address as of Tuesday, one day alive, one bag, one hat, one pair of gloves that do not fit, and one watch that still keeps perfect time. It is a start. It is a poor one, but I have started worse jobs than this on a Monday and finished them by Friday.
